title: Match the bulb to the battery
story: You have a 6 V lantern battery and a drawer of bulbs. Every bulb is printed with the voltage and current it was designed for, and when hot it behaves like a fixed resistor: a 1.5 V 0.3 A bulb is 5 Ω, a 6 V 0.5 A bulb is 12 Ω, a 12 V 0.25 A bulb is 48 Ω and a 24 V 0.1 A bulb is 240 Ω. Put the bulb in the socket that shines at its rated brightness without burning out. A bulb is happy near its rated current and power.

goals.label: bulb turns between 2.5 and 3.5 W into light and heat

hints: Pick the bulb whose printed voltage matches the battery's voltage.
Preview of Phase 03: current = voltage / resistance, and power = voltage x current.
The 5 Ω bulb would take 6 / 5 = 1.2 A, four times what it was built for. The 240 Ω bulb only gets 0.025 A and barely glows.
